junction.name: 4th Avenue South & South Jackson Street, Seattle

claims.text: 4th Avenue South & South Jackson Street had 19 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are 4th Avenue South & South Jackson Street's own: the city's record places 278 of the 319 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $1.3 million a year.
71% of crashes here were recorded as “angles” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
71% of crashes here were recorded as “entering at angle” crashes, against 16% at the city's worst crash locations.
66% of crashes here were recorded as “motor vehicle struck motor vehicle, front end at angle” crashes, against 43% at the city's worst crash locations.

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.

Backplates with Retroreflective Borders would avoid about 0.6 crashes a year (CMF 1410, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $195,000 a year; check on site: an entry on yellow or red.

Pavement Friction Management would avoid about 0.5 crashes a year (CMF 195, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $164,000 a year; check on site: the pavement's friction is low now (wet-road crashes alone do not show it).

The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 2nd Avenue Extension South, 4th Avenue South, 5th Avenue South, South Jackson Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
